To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness of mobile Internet banking are positively related to consumers’ intention to adopt this service.

the factors influencing consumers’ intention to adopt mobile Internet banking in India are trust, perceived risk, perceived usefulness, and subjective norms, with trust and perceived usefulness being the most important factors.
the perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness and perceived risk have positive effects on intention to use mobile banking in India.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding consumers’ intention to adopt mobile Internet banking.
understanding the antecedents of consumers’ intention to adopt mobile Internet banking and the role of perceived risk in this adoption process.

understanding the antecedents of intention to use mobile banking in India, with a focus on the role of the technology acceptance model (TAM) and the theory of planned behavior (TPB) in explaining the intention to use mobile internet banking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, mobile banking is a very important tool for financial inclusion.
the study has identified the factors that predict the intention of consumers to use mobile Internet Banking.
mobile Internet banking adoption is influenced by the perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived risk, perceived security, trust, and perceived enjoyment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model of mobile banking adoption that is consistent with the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behavior.
the use of mobile Internet banking is influenced by perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and trust in the mobile banking provider.
the adoption of mobile Internet banking is driven by perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microfinance institutions should concentrate their marketing efforts on consumers’ perceived benefits, perceived risks, trust, and perceived control.
mobile Internet banking in India is still in the early stages of adoption, and the adoption rate is still low, especially among rural and semi-rural consumers.

mobile Internet banking is a viable option for the Indian microfinance industry, and that the industry should concentrate its marketing efforts on factors such as perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and trust in mobile Internet banking.
